..
Pleasant weather of isolated showers and light to gentle
northeast to east winds look to continue in the short-term forecast.
Island-effect showers and isolated thunderstorms during the
afternoons will be the main concern for Guam through the weekend. 
Although there is a background trade-wind pattern over the region, 
wind speeds may subside enough for a light to gentle wind pattern 
over Guam, therefore allowing these showers to grow directly overhead
instead of advecting offshore. As for next week, model guidance 
indicates a potential tropical disturbance bringing increasing shower
and thunderstorm chances. The forecast reflects only scattered 
showers of 30 percent and a slight chance of thunderstorms for now, 
but this will likely be increased as model solutions converge on 
timing and intensity over the next few days. Those with interests in 
the Marianas should keep a close eye on the forecast over the next 
several days. Although we've had a lull in tropical cyclone activity,
this should be a reminder that the Marianas are in peak typhoon 
season, so maintaining a background state of preparedness is crucial.

Marine...
Light to gentle northeasterlies tonight will turn to the east on 
Saturday. The primary east trade swell is expected for the next 
several days as the west swell continues to subside. Combined seas of
3 to 4 ft as well as a moderate risk of rip currents along east and 
north facing reefs will persist for the next few days. Next week, 
swells may increase by a few feet or so if the aforementioned 
tropical disturbance materializes. Consequently, surf and sea heights
may approach hazardous conditions, so this situation will continue 
to be monitored.

Tropical Systems...
A weak circulation, Invest 99W, is centered east of Majuro near 
7N175E. 99W is currently rated sub-low, meaning development is not
expected over the next few days. Latest model guidance shows 99W
moving slowly west, then northwest, passing over the far northern
CNMI late next week. Invest 99W will be monitored closely over the
coming days for signs that it is becoming more organized. Islands in
the northern Marshall Islands and the Marianas should monitor
forecasts for any possible changes to expected movement or
development of Invest 99W.

Eastern Micronesia...
The key features affecting eastern Micronesia this afternoon are the
monsoon trough and Invest 99W. The monsoon trough will maintain a 
moist monsoonal flow across eastern Micronesia, keeping a wet 
pattern across Pohnpei and Kosrae through the next few days. For
Majuro, Invest 99W, located to the east near 7N175E will continue to
produce POPs from 30 to 50 percent through the weekend. As 99W moves
off to the northwest, it will pull the monsoon trough out of the
area. Therefore, POPs are expected to drop down into the 20 percent
range early next week.

A fairly benign marine pattern has returned to Pohnpei and will
continue across Kosrae and Majuro waters. Winds have died down at
Pohnpei and the Small Craft Advisory was allowed to expire. Seas look
to fall from near 7 feet at Pohnpei to around 4 to 5 feet over the
next 1 to 2 days. Seas will remain below 5 to 6 feet at Majuro and 
Kosrae. 

Western Micronesia...
There remains a Small Craft Advisory for Chuuk through 5 PM ChST
Saturday.

There are three main feature affecting the region, first the monsoon
flow, second a broad circulation to the south of Guam, and a low
pressure system around 5S170E, south of Eastern Micronesia. The
interaction between the western flank of the broad circulation and 
the monsoon flow is located around Palau and Yap. This interaction 
is producing low-end scattered showers bringing some much needed 
rain. This interaction is weakening and expected to move westward 
over the next day or so. 

The second interaction region is produced by the eastern flank of 
the broad circulation, the monsoon flow and a low pressure system 
south of the equator. This is producing a convergence axis from 
EQ144E northeastward through Chuuk Lagoon and extending northeast to 
near 12N157E. This interaction region is expected to elongate and
tilt to a more east-west bearing over the next several days as the
circulations move westward. This will keep numerous showers in the 
forecast for Chuuk for most of the forecast period and bring 
increasing showers into the forecast for Palau and Yap for next week.

Altimetry shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet for much of Yap State.
The primary swell for Palau and Yap is from the west, while the 
primary at Chuuk is from the south generated by the previously
mentioned low pressure system. Winds near Palau and Yap are light to
moderate, while at Chuuk they are gentle to fresh with frequent 
gusts to strong. A Maritime ship observation of 20 kt did confirm 
the sustained winds. Wind conditions along the second interaction 
region are expected to remain hazardous to small craft operations 
through at least Saturday afternoon.
